page: Microsoft Azure D2ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadsv7 family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical AMD EPYC 9V45 core running at 4.5 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture with Hyper-Threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB per core, and includes 118 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Virtualization is managed via Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark data indicates highly polarized performance characteristics. The server achieves top-tier results in single-core operations, including stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core scores, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Conversely, multi-core and multi-threaded performance is weak, as shown in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average, while small-block cached read bandwidth is weak.

The primary tradeoff of the D2ads_v7 is its strong single-thread execution speed contrasted against limited multi-threaded capacity due to its 2-vCPU hardware constraint. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, it offers a low-cost entry point to high-frequency AMD EPYC cores with dedicated CPU allocation and fast local NVMe storage. This profile is appropriate for lightweight workloads requiring high single-thread throughput but low parallel processing demands, such as basic text processing, simple single-threaded scripts, and low-traffic web serving.
